components.name: Decision Card
components.description: What he wants to do, why, the facts, the change behind a disclosure, and the yes and no with how they may be given.
components.html:
Let Barnaby order parts from your suppliers

To order ten pairs of brake pads from Madison for tomorrow's brake job.

Each time
He still asks you before he does it.
A new key needs a click, not a spoken yes.

narrative.overview: Barnaby's display is the one part of the product that is the app, so it is a real professional app, played straight: the conventions of Mail, Linear, Things 3 and the Claude desktop app, at their craft level, light by default. Nothing is a costume. Barnaby lives in the details: the bell tile, one brass accent, his words in every label and empty state, approvals that read like a colleague asking before he does something, and a voice control that feels native.
keyCharacteristics: Light white canvas, a warm-neutral inspector, hairlines; one soft shadow, only on the card that needs an answer.
Segoe UI throughout (Variable on Windows 11), one fixed scale; mono only for code and technical names.
The current answer is the largest text on screen (22px); history steps back to 18px in a softer ink.
Plain words first everywhere; the technical record is one disclosure away, never in the way.
Brass means "Barnaby" or "your turn", and nothing else.

rules.name: The Brass Rule
rules.body: Brass appears only on his mark, the waiting and listening states, focus and selection. If brass shows up anywhere else, it is decoration and comes out.

rules.name: The Never-Colour-Alone Rule
rules.body: Every state carries an icon and a word: a tick and "You said yes", a key and "Asks first", a no-entry sign and "Kept shut".

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: One family carries every word; scale and weight make the hierarchy. Mono is for code only.

rules.name: The Fixed Scale Rule
rules.body: Sizes are fixed pixels, not fluid: a pixel on the shop's 19-inch 1440×900 panel is as large as on a 24-inch 1080p screen, so nothing shrinks for the smaller screen.

rules.name: The One Raised Thing Rule
rules.body: Only a card that needs an answer casts a real shadow. Never a zero-offset glow.

dos: Do speak in the household's words on every surface the owner sees; technical names only in Details, "See the change" and "Show technical names".
Do say the status as a sentence in the present tense ("Looking at repair jobs due on Tue 24 Nov").
Do keep every yes and no in the thread, naming the thing, not its arguments.
Do keep the decision reachable: the card's footer docks while the card runs past the fold.
Do give every state an icon and a word; keep body text at ink or ink-2.
Do honour reduced motion (all animation off) and keep transitions at 150-220ms.
donts: Don't add themes or costumes: road signs, tickets, liveries, paper, enamel, brass gradients.
Don't bring back the AI tell: dark navy and brass, italic serif bot voice, bubbles left and right, status pills, a monospace live trace.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading, or a capsule around a state word.
Don't use brass for anything but his mark, the waiting and listening states, focus and selection.
Don't run more than one moving indicator at a time.
Don't promise what the app can't do: there is no way to take a key back yet, so no card says there is.
Don't call Barnaby's 3 new tests Theo's: "Theo's 19 checks still pass, and so do the 3 new ones."
